**Lemma · Scaling a row scales its evaluation.** Evaluating a complex scalar multiple of a row against data scales the row's evaluation by that scalar. [`ev_smul`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/RelAxis.lean#L171).

**Lemma · Row evaluation commutes with finite sums.** Evaluating a finite sum of rows against data gives the sum of their evaluations. [`ev_sum`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/RelAxis.lean#L176).

**Lemma · Strain rows read gradient coefficients.** Within the stored coefficient degrees, evaluating a strain-coordinate row on true field data gives the corresponding gradient-mode basis coefficient. [`ev_strain`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/RelAxis.lean#L181).

**Lemma · An extra row reads its strip datum.** Within the stored degree range, evaluating an extra-coordinate row on true field data gives the corresponding extra value. [`ev_extra`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/RelAxis.lean#L188).

**Lemma · The selected zero mode has value zero.** If the layout's zero-mode option selects a mode, that mode's underlying integer is zero. [`zeroMode_val`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/RelAxis.lean#L195).

**Lemma · From flux to a coefficient relation.** On an axis-touching cell with valid bases, the displayed flux identity and weighted integrability make the outer flux minus its two finite radial coefficient expansions vanish. [`hbase`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/RelAxis.lean#L205).

**Lemma · Strain rows read coefficient sums.** Evaluating a weighted finite sum of strain rows on true field data gives the same weighted sum of gradient-mode coefficients. [`ev_strain_sum`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/RelAxis.lean#L259).

**Lemma · Negated strain rows read negated modes.** Evaluating the weighted sum of negated strain rows on true data gives the weighted basis coefficients of the negated gradient mode. [`ev_negstrain_sum`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/RelAxis.lean#L266).

**Theorem · Each axis relation annihilates true data.** Assuming axis-weighted mode integrability and the zero-mode axis flux identity, every axis relation row of a valid cell layout evaluates to zero on admissible true field data. [`relAxis_main`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/RelAxis.lean#L279).

**Theorem · Axis flux supplies relation rows.** The axis-mode integrability and axis-flux propositions together imply the axis-relation proposition. [`relAxis_of`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/Breakdown/FracCell/RelAxis.lean#L333).

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.modeRadia.text: This closes the CellFormula proposition from RelRadialCoef; the same local name in ModeRadialPartsA closes the different CellAnalysis proposition from ResolvedEnergySt.

Breakdown.CellCert.Spectral.shapeGradCoe.text: The angular coefficient uses max(r, innerRadius) in its denominator. On a positive-radius cell this agrees with the intended inverse-radius coefficient, while the definition stays total outside that cell.

Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.harmonicWei.text: The horizontal and vertical Fourier energies are divided by (|k|+1/2)² and (|k|+3/2)² respectively, and multiplied by the spatial radius squared. These shifted denominators are part of the definition.

Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.ClassInvers.text: No theorem with this exact interface as its named result and no theorem referring to its name were found in the supplied library. Its universal requirement with constant 2/3 is distinct from inverseSquareConst_two, which supplies InverseSquareConstStatement with constant 2.

Breakdown.FracInternal.FrameInverseSquar.text: The proposition assumes the stated vanishing at the centre. Its name does not by itself assert oddness of the function on the whole interval.

Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.inverseSqua.text: The parameter is the norm constant H=2 in InverseSquareConstStatement; the squared-energy inequality therefore contains H²=4.

Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.SixthPowerC.text: No theorem with this exact interface as its named result and no theorem referring to its name were found in the supplied library. This records the status of the named interface; it does not assert that the mathematical estimate is false.

Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.RotationLea.text: This uses the totalized integral and ENNReal.toReal conventions, so the identity alone does not assert a finite L2 norm.

Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.RowModeGrad.text: The totalized integral and ENNReal.toReal conventions do not by themselves assert that the field has finite L2 norm.

Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.ExtendSegme.text: The supplied source slice has no exact named provider or consumer of this proposition; this is a declared interface, not a proved result in this file.

Breakdown.CellCert.Reduction.ClassCoverS.text: There is no exact named provider or consumer in the supplied slice; GivenModelCover.classCover_of is a specialized analogue with mesh, model and harmonic-cover assumptions, not a proof of this generic interface.

fidelity_held: This guide describes each declaration on its own terms. Comparisons of the Lean with the paper's numbered statements are on the paper, index and full-account pages.

families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).
